description: Measured by the OptionParser session: per-literal keying of returned arguments costs about +6.5% compile work per additional distinct call of the same function. Evidence: probes /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/p/distinct1.fz, distinct2.fz, distinct4.fz, distinct8.fz (1, 2, 4, 8 OptionParser.parse calls that differ only in their literal arguments), each with its telemetry (.jsonl) and canonical backend dump (.canon) beside it; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/p/byfn.py groups activation keys by function. The round-one page /Users/j5n/Workspace/optionparser-compile-cost.html, table 'What remains', records the per-function counts: Keyword.get/3 takes 10-12 keys and normalize_* similar, one per call-site literal; this is the returned-axis rule working as written (call sites x returning functions, linear). Concordant with fz-y6w (accumulator fanout) and fz-sc8.127 (a protocol callback's non-receiver arguments are keyed only where an implementation returns them): check whether one rule covers all three before building.
title: A returned argument is keyed by its type, not by each literal
